piezas.titular: Anthropic proposes organising AI agents' memory into four layers with a periodic review
piezas.entradilla: An Anthropic research text describes how to give an agent memory between sessions, and a teacher in the group has adapted their own system to that idea and explains it in an article with instructions.
cuerpo: AI agents for the computer, such as Claude Code, remember nothing from one session to the next unless they are given some way of doing so. On 6 November Anthropic published “[The components of agent memory](https://www.anthropic.com/research/components-of-agent-memory)”, which arranges that memory into four layers: transcripts, a searchable record of what the agent has done; memory notes, which the agent writes during sessions; representations, ordered structures built from the notes, such as a wiki of linked pages; and injected context, a small layer loaded at the start of each session that must be kept short because overly long instructions reduce how well the agent follows them.

The text adds an offline review, which it calls “dreaming”: the agent goes over its transcripts to cross-check the notes, correct errors, build representations and decide what is preloaded in future sessions. The authors warn that this review consumes computing power and should be focused on what is likely to change.

Juan José de Haro, author of the blog Bilateria, has adapted his personal system to this structure and explains it in the article “[Agentes de IA que aprenden mientras duermen](https://educacion.bilateria.org/agentes-de-ia-que-aprenden-mientras-duermen)” (AI agents that learn while they sleep), published on 7 November. He proposes a short profile, agent notes with an index, a project wiki with decision logs and the saved conversations as raw material, with a daily review that only writes a proposal: the agent checks each point before applying it and changes to the profile require the person’s approval. It includes a prompt for asking the agent itself to set the system up.

The article points out limits that matter to anyone weighing it up for a school: saved conversations contain sensitive information, the review can make mistakes, and each tool’s memory is not shared with the others. On what student data an agent should be able to see and remember, [the paper has already published a report](pieza:2026-10-31/agentes-ia-permisos-datos-alumnado).

piezas.titular: Holmio turns the periodic table into a daily detective game
piezas.entradilla: Each day brings a new case with 118 suspects, the chemical elements, and six accusations to find the culprit; according to its author, no registration is required.
cuerpo: [Holmio](https://holmio.elprofedelabata.es/) is a daily deduction game, in the style of Wordle but with a noir setting, for reviewing the elements of the periodic table. You read the case report, accuse an element and, if you are wrong, choose a clue to keep investigating. You have six accusations to find the culprit.

Besides the case of the day, the website offers an archive for playing earlier cases and free practice with a random element that does not count towards the archive. It has light and dark modes and lets you share your result as an image.

It was presented in Vibe Coding Educativo by Dani García, who explains that he made it with Claude Code in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks or server of its own, and publishes it on GitHub Pages; the website is signed by El profe de la bata. According to its author, the most work went into the content: a case for each of the 118 elements with data checked against sources. He asks users to tell him about bugs or ideas for the classroom. [Another activity by El profe de la bata, on the gravitational field, has already appeared in the paper](pieza:2026-11-03/misiones-orbitales).

piezas.titular: Incluxat brings the guidance from educational psychology reports to the conservatoire
piezas.entradilla: An AI assistant adapts to music education guidance designed for mainstream schools, with its supporting documentation published so it can be reviewed.
cuerpo: The guidance in educational psychology reports is usually written for compulsory education, whereas in a conservatoire instrument lessons are one-to-one and assessment takes the form of performances. [Incluxat](https://jlmirallesb.github.io/incluxat/proyecto/), created by José Luis Miralles Bono, is an assistant that translates that guidance into the conservatoire context.

It is offered as a Copilot agent of the Generalitat Valenciana, for staff in its schools, and as a Gemini Gem in a public version. It includes a knowledge base in Spanish and Valencian with Valencian regulations, support measures and examples by subject, instructions for setting it up yourself and a public repository. The website recommends testing the assistant with a control question before relying on it and not entering students’ personal data. The author is looking for conservatoires to try it and report problems.
Miralles Bono also shared other materials and apps of his in the group, including tools for conservatoire timetables.
